flashcard_questions.q: Which Roman god does Macbeth appeal to as he stares at his bloody hands?
Why does appealing to a pagan god matter for a Jacobean audience?
flashcard_questions.a: It signals Macbeth is spiritually cut off from Christianity by his regicide.

flashcard_questions.q: What does ‘incarnadine’ mean in Macbeth’s speech about the seas?
Which technique is Macbeth using when he says his hand would redden whole oceans?
What does Lady Macbeth mean by taunting Macbeth with ‘a heart so white’?
flashcard_questions.a: She is accusing him of cowardice.

flashcard_questions.q: Which line shows Lady Macbeth believing guilt can simply be washed off?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘A little water clears us of this deed.’

flashcard_questions.q: Which Act 5 line shows Lady Macbeth destroyed by the guilt she once dismissed?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘All the perfumes of Arabia will not sweeten this little hand.’

flashcard_questions.q: What is foreshadowing in a play?
flashcard_questions.a: A technique where the writer hints at plot developments still to come.
Someone who uses deliberately ambiguous language to deceive without technically lying.

flashcard_questions.q: Who waits on the other side of the gate while the knocking continues?
Which word does Macduff repeat three times on finding Duncan’s body?
What might Macduff’s triple repetition of that cry echo?
flashcard_questions.a: The Holy Trinity, making the murder a sin of cosmic proportions.

flashcard_questions.q: Which metaphor does Macduff use for Duncan as the source of a royal bloodline?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘The fountain of your blood is stopped.’

flashcard_questions.q: Which precious colours does Macbeth use to describe Duncan’s murdered body?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘His silver skin laced with his golden blood.’

flashcard_questions.q: Which metaphor does Donalbain use for the hidden danger around him?

notes: 15 cards: 6 quotation-recall fronts, 3 quotation-to-effect (‘heart so white’, the Trinity echo, the pagan appeal), 2 term-to-definition (foreshadowing, equivocator), 2 single-word technique/word cards (hyperbole, ‘incarnadine’), 2 plot-fact cards (Neptune, Macduff at the gate). ‘Motif’, ‘comic relief’ and ‘usurpation’ dropped — the first two would interfere with the technique cards kept, the third is not tested in the content. The Porter’s three sinners were left out because the only honest card would be an enumeration. All quotations verbatim from the lesson content.
